# §A — Purpose, authority and dependency boundary
**CHD-3.4 · SPEC V3.4 · authored specification, not a deployed service.**
> **REVISION NOTICE — CHD-3.4 supersedes CHD-3.3.** This section replaces competing package authority and ambiguous supported-status claims. G-01/G-10 select one release. D-039 remains binding. Revised content carries change bars in the rendered edition.

## A.1 Purpose and scope
CHD is a controller service that turns a VP goal into accountable, evidenced work. The operating hierarchy is **VP → director → manager → supervisor → foreman → worker**. The VP defines the outcome and constraints. The director decomposes it and owns final acceptance. Managers own assigned slices and delegate bounded decisions. Supervisors apply prescribed conditions and coordinate foremen. Foremen organize execution and verify workers. Workers execute bounded units and report.
The control plane contains objectives, assignments, rooms, tickets, requests, sends, attempts, execution reservations, policy snapshots, reports and audit. Work-plane repositories, worktrees, test runs and artifacts remain external; CHD stores accountable references rather than another copy of the product. Coding and non-coding goals use the same hierarchy. Payment, publication, production changes and external sending require separately authorized capabilities.

## A.2 Authority and package resolution
Confirmed owner decisions govern. The selected integration contract is `build-spec/INTEGRATION.md` at the specification root. This edition applies its corrections to readable handbook content and explicitly identifies new specification-level lifecycle completions. The root integration verdict remains NOT YET BUILDABLE until the residual runtime, native and storage gates close. An authored edge, valid schema, generated document or fixture PASS is not implementation, runtime evidence or owner acceptance.
TABLE 1.1-1 — Domain authority and supersession
| Domain | Selected source relative to this edition | Boundary | |---|---|---| | Current configuration | `contracts/config.schema.json`; §17 configuration reference | v4 activation only; v2/v3 are historical migration inputs, never silent defaults | | HTTP request/response contract | `contracts/openapi.yaml`; generated operation cards in §24 | 59 operations retain all OP-001..OP-048 mappings; generic historical tool envelopes are retired | | Gateway identity | `contracts/gateway-identity.md`; §E | Scoped canonical profile/send/attempt/target/credential identity; native allocation transport remains G-04 | | Lifecycle | `tables/lifecycle-34.json`; §§B/J/K and §25 | Six typed record machines; replaces conflicting old send/objective projections; storage writer encoding remains G-12 | | Restore policy | D-039; §§I/L/N | Current permissions on every restore/replacement; source snapshots remain history | | Storage | §G requirements and §21 dependency mapping | Memory HTTP facts selected; competing HB/VB shapes and completion proposals remain reference-only pending G-12 | | CLI and MCP | §18 | Existing Muster; no invented CHD command framework; IF-06/IF-07 gate full MCP publication | | Stack and generation | §§20/22 | Pinned generation transport and read views, not implemented controller logic | | Acceptance | §P | One current falsifying conformance specification; old fixtures are evidence only |
`BOOK.yaml` owns reading order, section addresses, figure registry, source hashes, revision notices and change-bar instructions. It is the authoring manifest, not a fabricated final-folio index. The render task derives physical folios from actual output and stamps `CHD3.4A-03-BLOCK I-(1..N)` and `SPEC V3.4`. Missing manifest inputs are build errors. No prior HTML/PDF is an input to this edition. Historical sheets remain preserved, not silently overwritten.

## A.3 Responsibility and trust boundaries
TABLE 1.3-1 — Producers, authority and prohibited shortcuts
| Actor | Owned effect | Prohibited shortcut | |---|---|---| | VP | Goal, grant ceiling, configured human decision | A goal does not grant all external capabilities | | Director | Decomposition, scoped delegation, evidence-based acceptance | Cannot treat reports, approvals or delivery ACKs as each other | | Manager | Assigned scope, supervisors and parent roll-up | Cannot expand scope or auto-pass incomplete criteria | | Supervisor | Conditional verification and foreman coordination | Does not prescribe worker organization or invent policy | | Foreman | Managed dispatch, worker organization and verification | No direct gateway credentials or control-store writes | | Worker | Bounded work and correlated report | No sibling control or acceptance authority | | Controller | Authorization, validation, durable transitions, reservations and external dispatch | No unfenced store writes; no inferred native capabilities | | Scheduler | Timed callback to controller | No direct gateway calls or separate admission ledger | | Hermes | Native profiles, sessions, history, memory, learning and model fallback | Not CHD ticket, grant or objective authority | | DuckBrain | Namespaced memory storage at the selected pin | No assumed multi-key transaction, CAS or coherent concurrent pagination | | Crier | Authenticated scoped delivery between independent systems | Connectivity never grants VP authority | | boardctl-compatible client | Ticket read/import/export view | No second ticket ledger or pull/commit synchronization authority |
FIGURE 1.3-1 — Control and work-plane boundary. Snapshot: 2026-11-11.
The controller validates an incoming request, commits its obligation through the selected storage boundary, reserves attempt/run capacity and targets a committed native identity. The archive path is separate and remains capability-gated. Crier and scheduler are inputs, never writers of control authority.
1. An authenticated VP, scheduler or peer request enters its scoped controller door. 2. The controller resolves authority and validates the exact wire schema. 3. The storage adapter commits the request and reservation under current writer authority. 4. A version-bound native adapter allocates or resolves the target; the controller commits that identity before first delivery. 5. The worker returns a correlated report. Verification and runtime-stop evidence remain distinct. 6. Failure of writer authority withholds mutation and dispatch. Unknown remote outcome retains reservation and identity for reconciliation.

## A.4 Distinct identities and terminology
TABLE 1.4-1 — Identity, state and evidence vocabulary
| Term | Meaning | |---|---| | room/thread | Ordered permissioned work log / reply tree, not native transcript | | request_id | Caller request/replay correlation; aliases use canonical route identity | | send_id | Logical owed work, potentially spanning multiple attempts | | attempt_id | One immutable dispatch target episode; exact transport retry retains it; authorized replacement/resume creates a successor | | native allocation/session | Runtime-owned identity recorded in a profile-bound bond before delivery | | run/reservation | Execution and authoritative capacity ownership; not the number of bonds | | report | Correlated content answering work; neither acceptance nor stop proof | | wait/approval | Recorded dependency and configured decision; timers confer no permission | | grant | One scoped authority record; use, grant-use, meta-grant and create are independent | | snapshot | Policy bound to a live session; ordinary continuation/restart preserves it | | archive | Committed payload and checkpoint metadata, not active runtime or effective permissions | | objective/assignment | Separate state machines; an accepted child does not by itself complete the objective | | specified | Contract text exists; no runtime claim | | fixture-validated | Offline structural/model inputs passed; no system-under-test claim | | runtime-verified | Version-bound observed service effects and negative traces passed | | owner-accepted | Explicit owner decision recorded separately |

## A.5 Required and optional capability boundary
Core CHD requires safe hierarchy execution, typed controller operations, policy enforcement, durable reservations, correlation, restore and acceptance. These requirements are not removed to make the package green. G-04/G-06/G-07 native allocation, stop and archive contracts remain release gates. G-12 atomic fencing, lease/snapshot binding and writer migrations remain release gates. Full MCP exposure remains blocked on IF-06/IF-07. The integration's other OPEN findings retain authoring and QA dispositions in §26.
Temporary workers with all required explicit fields are specified. Missing model, provider, context, lifetime, workspace, profile, credential, capacity or retention fails with the field path. Unsettled defaults block only defaulted creation. Lower-tier creation requires explicit configured create authority and provisioning/readback; dispatching an existing worker does not create a profile. Project memory and external domain connectors are optional, separately authorized adapters. Neither may become control-state authority.
Read-only, immediate and scheduled readiness are independent outputs. Scheduler outage alone does not disable otherwise-ready controller-local immediate work. No immediate/write readiness exists without the required storage and runtime capabilities. A maintenance or degraded-state screen must name the blocked capability, not claim a single global healthy flag.

## A.6 Dependency ledger and reference interpretation
The source inventory records exact hashes of the integration snapshot and this edition. DuckBrain is pinned to `972aeb0023973b2d62186a748eab5ccede2dd0f8`; Muster to `3b6de28153f7726a81ebc1b10fa70d382d48c410`. §22 carries the selected Go and library pins. These are compatibility baselines, not statements about a live deployment. Native Hermes adapter/API/export versions remain unresolved; a guessed URL is not a capability probe.
Historical source paths printed in reference chapters identify provenance under the specification root. They do not override the authority table. Missing or contradictory native/storage definitions stay explicit OPEN gates. The book never equates a complete source inventory with a complete implementation.
